summary: Automated scientific discovery has the potential to advance understanding of disease mechanisms and accelerate identification of early disease markers. Manual data annotation is infeasible at population scale, motivating methods that automatically extract pre-defined phenotypes in multimodal and unstructured clinical data.
takeaways: This limitation extends to agentic AI systems that use these tools to query population-scale data.
In contrast, foundation models (FMs) trained on large volumes of clinical data can perform tasks beyond their training objectives.
This suggests their latent embeddings may represent novel or unexplored features that could yield insights into disease mechanisms, yet such latent features remain difficult to interpret.
